note: Searched all of agent/ (app, tools, migrations, manifest, config, README) for retrieval, search, embedding, vector, chunk and memory. There is no vector store, but the agent keeps a persistent corpus (Postgres dept_notes, written by memory_write and read by memory_read) and loads it into model context across runs. Ingested documents (documents table, ingest.py) are a second store. manifest.yaml:91 'retrieval: none' and read-by-id in documents.py:24 do not cover dept_notes, so the N/A condition fails. The tenant filter on memory_read comes from a model-supplied argument, so R04.3 fails.

checks.note: memory_write validates note content, kind and length but does not check the writer against a named list. It only records writer_instance. ingest.py does check an HMAC from one gateway. The docs show no named-writer allowlist, so this is unclear rather than proven failing.

dept_notes.source_doc_id is optional and model-supplied, so source is not guaranteed on every chunk. There is no per-chunk access-permission field beyond business_unit. The documents table has no trust-level column.

The tenant comes from a model-supplied argument and falls back to the caller's tenant only when it is absent. The tool description invites cross-unit lookups, and no code verifies a shared-services role.

Search excludes quarantined and expired notes, and ops can UPDATE the quarantined flag in SQL. No app code revokes access or expires documents, and no cache invalidation exists. No caches were found, and no test shows the removal time.

violates: Enforce the requesting tenant's access when searching
Search applies the requesting tenant's access filter at query time
